titleEn: For centuries, bird migration was a mystery – a tech revolution is changing that, and could help save these amazing creatures
titleZh: 鸟类迁徙曾是千古谜团：追踪技术如何改变认知并帮助保护它们
method: Machine reference translation with paragraph alignment; not manually certified.

paragraphs.en: For more than 2,000 years, scientists have scratched their heads over one of the most basic mysteries of the natural world: Where do birds go?
paragraphs.zh: 2,000多年来，科学家们一直在为自然界最基本的谜团之一而挠头：鸟类去哪里了？

paragraphs.en: Billions of birds appear and disappear with the seasons every year. Early naturalists offered explanations for the disappearances that today seem fantastical: Birds transformed into other species, one theory went. Others suggested they hibernated underwater or even migrated to the moon.
paragraphs.zh: 每年有数十亿只鸟类随着季节的变化而出现和消失。早期的博物学家对鸟类的消失给出了一些解释，而这些解释在今天看来似乎是天方夜谭：一种理论认为，鸟类变成了其他物种。另一种理论则认为，鸟类在水下冬眠，甚至迁徙到了月球上。

paragraphs.en: The truth, that these small animals were traveling thousands of miles across the planet, must once have seemed just as improbable.
paragraphs.zh: 事实上，这些小动物在地球上旅行了数千英里，这在过去一定也是不可能的。

paragraphs.en: Then, in the early 1800s, dramatic evidence emerged supporting the theory of migration. White storks began appearing in Germany with African arrows embedded in their bodies. These birds became known as pfeilstörche, or “arrow storks.” They provided compelling evidence that birds disappearing from Europe were traveling all the way to Africa and back.
paragraphs.zh: 然后，在19世纪初，支持迁徙理论的戏剧性证据出现了。白色开始出现在德国，它们的身体里插着非洲的箭。这些鸟后来被称为“箭鹳”。它们提供了令人信服的证据，证明从欧洲消失的鸟类是一路旅行到非洲再回来的。

paragraphs.en: Almost two centuries later, scientists are still asking the same question, but our ability to answer it has been transformed.
paragraphs.zh: 差不多两个世纪过去了，科学家们仍然在问同样的问题，但我们回答这个问题的能力已经发生了变化。

paragraphs.en: For most of ornithological history, scientists understood migration through brief glimpses of a bird, a specimen collected somewhere else, or the rare instance of a banded bird recovered hundreds or thousands of miles from where it had been marked. From these fragments of intelligence, scientists reconstructed journeys that took place largely beyond their view.
paragraphs.zh: 在鸟类学史上的大部分时间里，科学家们通过对鸟类的短暂一瞥、从别处采集的标本，或者是罕见的有条纹的鸟类从标记的地方恢复到数百或数千英里的地方，来理解迁徙。科学家们从这些情报片段中重建了发生在他们视野之外的旅行。

paragraphs.en: Today, it’s possible to see the journeys themselves, almost in real time.
paragraphs.zh: 如今，人们几乎可以真实的地看到这些旅程。

paragraphs.en: A century of following birds
paragraphs.zh: 百年来的追随鸟群

paragraphs.en: Bird banding was the first tool used to attempt a systematic approach to connect these fragments of information. Since the early 1900s, researchers have placed uniquely numbered metal bands on birds and hoped someone, somewhere, would encounter them again.
paragraphs.zh: 鸟类环志是第一个尝试用系统的方法来连接这些信息碎片的工具。自20世纪初以来，研究人员就在鸟类身上放置了独特编号的金属带，希望有人在某处再次遇到它们。

paragraphs.en: Of more than 79 million birds banded, only about 6.5 million have been recovered. That generally told scientists just two things: where a bird was banded and where it was encountered again. Everything between them remained invisible.
paragraphs.zh: 在7900多万只被绑在一起的鸟类中，只有大约650万只被发现。这通常只能告诉科学家两件事：一只鸟是在哪里被绑在一起的，另一只鸟是在哪里被再次遇到的。它们之间的一切都是不可见的。

paragraphs.en: Over the past quarter-century or so, the tools used to determine where birds go have changed dramatically.
paragraphs.zh: 在过去25年左右的时间里，用来确定鸟类去向的工具发生了巨大的变化。

paragraphs.en: Tracking devices can now be carried by increasingly smaller birds, recording their movements and communicating with land-based receivers or satellites orbiting the earth. Testing stable isotopes in feathers and other tissues can reveal where a bird originated. Genetic testing can distinguish populations.
paragraphs.zh: 如今，越来越小的鸟类可以携带跟踪装置，记录它们的活动，并与地面接收器或绕地球运行的卫星进行通信。测试羽毛和其他组织中的稳定同位素可以揭示鸟类的起源。基因测试可以区分种群。

paragraphs.en: At the same time, the extraordinary growth of bird-watching and citizen science has created another revolution.
paragraphs.zh: 与此同时，观鸟和公民科学的非凡发展引发了另一场革命。

paragraphs.en: Millions of observations by bird-watchers submitted to eBird, an online database to record the birds they see, show the distribution and abundance of birds across a continent throughout the year in ways early ornithologists could scarcely have imagined.
paragraphs.zh: 鸟类观察者提交给eBird（一个记录他们看到的鸟类的在线数据库）的数百万份观察结果显示，鸟类在一个大陆上全年的分布和数量，以早期鸟类学家几乎无法想象的方式。

paragraphs.en: Collectively, these methods open an extraordinary new window into migratory birds and one of nature’s most remarkable behaviors: migration.
paragraphs.zh: 总之，这些方法打开了一扇非同寻常的新窗口，让我们得以了解候鸟和自然界最引人注目的行为之一：迁徙。

paragraphs.en: Discovering unknown migrations
paragraphs.zh: 发现未知迁移

paragraphs.en: More than 70% of North American bird species are migratory. Yet scientists have known surprisingly little about where specific populations go.
paragraphs.zh: 超过70%的北美鸟类是迁徙性的，然而科学家们对特定种群的迁徙所知甚少。

paragraphs.en: A species like the American robin may breed across thousands of miles of North America, with different breeding populations migrating to entirely different places for the winter. Birds breeding in one part of the continent may travel one route and encounter one set of environmental conditions, while members of the same species experience a completely different set of conditions along another route.
paragraphs.zh: 像美洲知更鸟这样的物种可能会在北美数千英里的范围内繁殖，不同的繁殖种群会迁徙到完全不同的地方过冬。在大陆的一个地区繁殖的鸟类可能会沿着一条路线行进，遇到一组环境条件，而同一物种的成员则会沿着另一条路线经历完全不同的一组环境条件。

paragraphs.en: These connections between where a bird breeds and where it spends the winter is called migratory connectivity. They are critical for understanding everything from the consequences of climate change on birds to how avian pathogens and diseases spread, to a species’ basic ecology.
paragraphs.zh: 鸟类繁殖地和过冬地之间的这种联系被称为迁徙连接。它们对于理解从气候变化对鸟类的影响到鸟类病原体和疾病的传播，再到物种的基本生态学等一切都至关重要。

paragraphs.en: We are ornithologists and conservation scientists who have spent almost 15 years along with a team of contributors compiling this rapidly expanding knowledge on bird movement into The Atlas of North America’s Migratory Birds. It is being published Nov. 3, 2026, by Princeton University Press, with all profits going to bird conservation and research in Latin America and the Caribbean. The atlas covers the latest information on seasonal movements for nearly 600 species and combines a century of bird-banding data with eBird observations, tracking studies, stable isotope testing, genetics and other sources of information.
paragraphs.zh: 我们是鸟类学家和保护科学家，花了将近15年的时间沿着与一个团队的贡献者一起，将这些关于鸟类迁徙的快速增长的知识汇编成了《北美候鸟地图集》。这本书将于2026年11月3日由普林斯顿大学出版社出版。所有收益将用于拉丁美洲和加勒比地区的鸟类保护和研究。该地图集涵盖了近600年来鸟类季节性活动的最新信息物种，并结合了一个世纪的鸟类带数据与电子鸟观察，跟踪研究，稳定同位素测试，遗传学和其他来源的信息。

paragraphs.en: What emerges is a picture of migratory birds that is both more complicated and more remarkable than the simple arrows pointing between breeding and wintering ranges on a map.
paragraphs.zh: 这幅候鸟的图像比地图上简单的箭头所指的繁殖和越冬范围更复杂，也更引人注目。

paragraphs.en: Consider the yellow-billed cuckoo. These birds breed over a wide range of the eastern two-thirds of the U.S. but migrate to a relatively small wintering area in the Gran Chaco region of northern Argentina, Paraguay and southern Bolivia.
paragraphs.zh: 以黄嘴杜鹃为例，这种鸟在美国东部三分之二的大范围内繁殖，但会迁徙到北方阿根廷、巴拉圭和玻利维亚南部的大查科地区一个相对较小的越冬区。

paragraphs.en: In contrast, peregrine falcons that breed in Alaska migrate almost directly south, dispersing across the Americas to wintering grounds that extend as far as southern South America.
paragraphs.zh: 相比之下，在阿拉斯加繁殖的游隼几乎直接向南迁徙，分散在美洲的越冬地，一直延伸到南美洲南部。

paragraphs.en: Discoveries like these are accumulating rapidly. Collectively, they amount to a renaissance in our understanding of animal movement never before imagined.
paragraphs.zh: 像这样的发现正在迅速积累。总的来说，它们相当于我们对动物运动的理解的复兴，这是以前从未想象过的。

paragraphs.en: Living masterpieces
paragraphs.zh: 活的杰作

paragraphs.en: The more clearly scientists can follow individual birds and populations across the planet, the more extraordinary these species can seem.
paragraphs.zh: 科学家们越能清楚地跟踪地球上的鸟类个体和种群，这些物种就越显得不同寻常。

paragraphs.en: Migratory birds such as the arctic tern and northern wheatear cross oceans, deserts and mountain ranges. Some, like the bar-tailed godwits, fly thousands of miles without stopping. Others, like the American redstart, return year after year to remarkably precise breeding and wintering locations.
paragraphs.zh: 像北极燕鸥和北方麦穗鸟这样的候鸟穿越海洋、沙漠和山脉。有些鸟，比如斑尾鹬，飞行数千英里不停歇。其他的，比如美洲红尾椋鸟，年复一年地回到非常精确的繁殖和越冬地点。

paragraphs.en: They navigate landscapes and respond to winds, weather, food and environmental conditions across enormous geographic scales.
paragraphs.zh: 它们在巨大的地理范围内导航景观，并对风、天气、食物和环境条件做出反应。

paragraphs.en: We see these species and their migrations as among evolution’s great living masterpieces. That’s why we combined science with natural history and artist John Anderton’s extraordinary illustrations of the birds themselves. The maps allow us to see where birds travel, and the art brings the species to life.
paragraphs.zh: 我们把这些物种和它们的迁徙看作是进化史上最伟大的杰作之一。这就是为什么我们把科学与自然历史结合在一起，艺术家约翰安德顿对鸟类本身的非凡插图。这些地图让我们看到鸟类的迁徙路线，而艺术则让这些物种栩栩如生。

paragraphs.en: Together, they make visible something that humans could only imagine for most of our history.
paragraphs.zh: 它们一起使人类在历史上的大部分时间里只能想象的东西变得可见。

paragraphs.en: A map for conservation
paragraphs.zh: 保护区地图

paragraphs.en: North America has lost about 3 billion birds during the past half-century, and many migratory species continue to decline.
paragraphs.zh: 在过去的半个世纪里，北美已经失去了大约30亿只鸟类，许多迁徙物种继续减少。

paragraphs.en: To understand why a population is declining and help save it, researchers need to understand the species’ entire annual cycle: its critical stopover habitats, wintering grounds and threats along its migration routes.
paragraphs.zh: 为了理解为什么一个种群正在下降并帮助拯救它，研究人员需要了解该物种的整个年度周期：其关键的中途停留栖息地，越冬地和沿着的威胁。

paragraphs.en: For much of the history of ornithology, scientists studied birds primarily during their breeding season. That made practical sense. Birds are conspicuous then – singing, defending territories, building nests and raising young.
paragraphs.zh: 在鸟类学的大部分历史中，科学家们主要在鸟类的繁殖季节研究它们。这是有实际意义的。鸟类在那时是引人注目的--唱歌、保卫领土、筑巢和养育后代。

paragraphs.en: But a migratory bird may spend only a few months of its life in its breeding grounds. Conditions such as weather, food availability and habitat quality encountered during migration can determine whether an individual survives to breed again.
paragraphs.zh: 但是，候鸟在繁殖地的生活可能只有几个月，在迁徙过程中遇到的天气、食物供应和栖息地质量等条件可以决定一个个体是否能生存下来再次繁殖。

paragraphs.en: Drought thousands of miles away can affect a bird’s condition months later. American redstarts depart later after dry winters and produce fewer young. Declining horseshoe crab populations in Delaware Bay have reduced food availability for migrating red knots, contributing to lower survival.
paragraphs.zh: 数千英里外的干旱会影响鸟类数月后的状况。美国红尾椋鸟在干燥的冬季后离开得更晚，繁殖的后代也更少。特拉华州湾的马蹄蟹数量减少，减少了迁徙红结的食物供应，导致存活率下降。

paragraphs.en: The power of people
paragraphs.zh: 人民的力量

paragraphs.en: All of this knowledge has accumulated because people value birds and have devoted enormous time and effort to understanding them.
paragraphs.zh: 所有这些知识的积累是因为人们重视鸟类，并投入了大量的时间和精力来了解它们。

paragraphs.en: For more than a century, thousands of bird-banders have woken up before the crack of dawn to set traps, carefully place bands on birds’ legs and release them, often knowing the chances of ever learning what happened to those individuals were exceedingly small.
paragraphs.zh: 世纪以来，成千上万的捕鸟者在黎明前醒来，设置陷阱，小心地在鸟的腿上绑上带子，然后把它们放出来，他们通常知道知道这些鸟身上发生了什么的机会非常小。

paragraphs.en: More recently, tracking technology has allowed researchers to follow individual birds across continents and oceans. Those tracks exist because scientists, students, technicians and others have spent countless hours attaching and recovering tags, and contributing and sharing their data.
paragraphs.zh: 最近，追踪技术使研究人员能够跨越大陆和海洋跟踪单个鸟类。这些轨迹的存在是因为科学家、学生、技术人员和其他人花费了无数时间来贴上和恢复标签，并贡献和分享他们的数据。

paragraphs.en: Today, millions of bird-watchers contribute observations that, thanks to advances in data science, allow us to watch migration unfold across an entire continent.
paragraphs.zh: 今天，数百万鸟类观察者提供了观察结果，由于数据科学的进步，使我们能够观察整个大陆的迁徙情况。

paragraphs.en: We have spent much of our careers documenting the decline of birds, and we know the challenges facing migratory species are formidable. But we also have hope for these creatures’ survival.
paragraphs.zh: 我们花了大量的时间来记录鸟类的衰落，我们知道迁徙物种面临的挑战是巨大的，但我们也对这些生物的生存抱有希望。

paragraphs.en: Scientists today know more about where migratory birds go, how populations are connected and what they encounter along the way than at any previous point in history. That knowledge is helping to identify where conservation efforts can make a difference for the future.
paragraphs.zh: 今天的科学家比历史上任何时候都更了解候鸟的去向、种群之间的联系以及它们在迁徙途中沿着遇到的情况。这些知识有助于确定保护工作在哪些方面可以为未来带来改变。
